correctness.rationale: Tree effective resistance is exactly the sum of reciprocal conductances on the unique path; hence diameter equals the largest sum of two hub-to-leaf radial resistances. For fixed radial resistance, strict convexity of the reciprocal-power expenditure uniquely selects each edge resistance. After normalizing by proposed diameter, the cost is a strictly convex function on pairwise-sum constraints. If all radii are at most 1/2, setting every radius to 1/2 is optimal. If one radius exceeds 1/2, all others must equal its complement and strict convexity reduces to one variable. The interior minimum exists iff its cost aggregate exceeds the sum of the others. Only one aggregate can satisfy this; equality is uniquely balanced. Scaling by the actual budget gives the claimed exact minimum and unrestricted edge-level uniqueness for every positive exponent, including concave conductance-pricing exponents. The exponent transition is proved by monotonicity of a finite sum of powers. The included standalone script passed 1256 rational-input, randomized direct-Laplacian and numerical optimization assertions, which corroborate but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: This work does not claim to originate minimax effective-resistance optimization. Ghosh–Boyd–Saberi explicitly formulate that as a general linear-budget convex SDP in the 2006 primary paper, while their exact tree allocation is for the sum rather than maximum of pair resistances. A relevant author-uploaded full-text tree-upgrading paper (Chepoi–Noltemeier–Vaxès) gives an LP for linearly priced shortening of fixed edge lengths, and therefore its decision variable and cost functional are not the reciprocal-conductance power-cost problem: applying the transformation would require a nonlinear cost that their LP does not treat. The Hambrusch–Lim edge-reduction paper remains an inaccessible plausible comparison and is expressly retained as risk. Published semantic findings about spider domination, curvature and effective-resistance flow-polytopes do not imply this exact all-price minimax network allocation by their statements. The original claimed contribution is the all-power-law, heterogeneous, uniquely optimal spider conductance formula and its one-dominant-arm threshold, not generic convexity or the physical resistance metric.

value.rationale: Worst-case pairwise effective resistance naturally quantifies worst source-to-sink performance in a branching resistive network, and assigning conductances under heterogeneous material prices is an actual design decision. The theorem classifies all independent edge allocations on any spider with arbitrary arm lengths and prices, establishes an unexpected one-dominant-arm rigidity and sharp aggregate threshold, and exhibits a genuine change in the unique optimum when the cost power changes on a fixed topology. The nonlinear concave-cost regime is also resolved analytically through convexity of the physical resistance variables. These are structural and scalable optimality facts, not a textbook substitution, arbitrary numerical slice, or modest isolated estimate.
